notes:
Space Engineers has no RCON and no text console on the dedicated server. Its only command channel is Keen's VRage Remote API, a JSON HTTP API served by the dedicated server itself. Enable it with RemoteApiEnabled, set RemoteApiPort (default 8080) and RemoteSecurityKey in SpaceEngineers-Dedicated.cfg or on the General tab of the dedicated-server GUI; all four names (RemoteApiEnabled, RemoteApiIP, RemoteApiPort, RemoteSecurityKey) are verified against Keen's own ModAPI reference for IMyConfigDedicated. A restart is required after changing them.

AUTH IS NOT A PLAIN HEADER TOKEN, despite auth.type 'header'. Every request carries 'Date: <UTC RFC1123>' and 'Authorization: <nonce>:<base64 HMAC-SHA1>'. The nonce is a single-use random string; the signed message is the request path INCLUDING basePath and any query string, then the nonce, then the date, each followed by CRLF (path + "\r\n" + nonce + "\r\n" + date + "\r\n"), hashed with the base64-DECODED RemoteSecurityKey as the key. Verified in three independent implementations: vrage_api (Python, build_headers), space-engineers (Node, lib/bridge.js opts) and space-engineers-exporter (Go, GetHMAC), and described in prose on Keen's own dedicated-servers page. auth.name is the header the result goes in.

COMMAND ENCODING: this game is commanded by HTTP, not by console text, so each command is written as '<METHOD> <path>' with the path RELATIVE TO basePath. Prepend basePath to get the real request line, e.g. listPlayers is GET http://<host>:8080/vrageremote/v1/session/players. say is the one command with a body: POST /session/chat carries the message as the whole JSON request body, i.e. a bare JSON string (Content-Type: application/json, body "hello everyone") - the {message} token after the path is that body, not a path segment or query parameter. Verified in both clients: vrage_api send_chat_message posts json=message, and the Node client sends {body: message} to the same path.

KICK IS NOT RECORDED. The two client codebases that implement a kick disagree and no primary source settles it: vrage_api sends POST /admin/kickedPlayers/{steamId} (DELETE to the same path to un-kick), while the Node client sends POST /admin/kickPlayers/{steamId} (no 'ed'). Only the GET listing /admin/kickedPlayers is agreed on, by vrage_api, the Node client and serap. POST /admin/kickedPlayers/{steamId} is the better candidate - it is REST-symmetric with bannedPlayers and promotedPlayers and with that GET listing - but it has a single source and one source contradicting it, so it fails the two-independent-sources bar and was removed rather than shipped as a silent 404. Probe both paths against a live server before adding a kick; until then ban/unban is the working moderation path.

Everything that IS recorded - GET /server, GET /session/players, POST and DELETE /admin/bannedPlayers/{steamId}, POST /session/chat - is agreed by two or more independent codebases (vrage_api, the space-engineers npm client, serap's endpoint list). GET /server/ping also exists and is a useful liveness check.

Ban takes no reason and no duration: the API ban is permanent until DELETE /admin/bannedPlayers/{steamId}. There is no motd command; MessageOfTheDay is a config property on IMyConfigDedicated, not a runtime command. The API also exposes promote/demote (POST/DELETE /admin/promotedPlayers/{steamId}), grid/asteroid/planet/floatingObject deletion, PATCH on session entities to stop them, and DELETE /server to stop the server.

playerParse reads the envelope the API always returns: {"data": {"Players": [{"SteamID": 76561198000000000, "DisplayName": "...", "FactionName": "...", "FactionTag": "...", "PromoteLevel": 4, "Ping": 69}]}, "meta": {...}}; the vrage_api README iterates exactly players["data"]["Players"] reading ["SteamID"] and ["DisplayName"]. SteamID is a JSON NUMBER, not a string, and it is a full 64-bit value - a client that parses it as a double will corrupt it, so read it as a big integer or as a raw string (the Node client pulls in json-bigint for precisely this reason).

PLAYER ID CAVEAT: the field is called SteamID, but since crossplay (EOS/Xbox) a connected player is not necessarily a Steam user, and Keen's own ModAPI notes that the Banned and Reserved config lists hold 'SteamId and Xbox live ids' as ulong. The pattern here is therefore a bare 64-bit decimal rather than the 7656119 Steam prefix, so non-Steam players still match.

NOT RECORDED: midspace's Admin Helper script mod adds in-game chat commands such as /kick and /ban, but that is a workshop mod and not part of the shipped server, so it is out of scope here.
